prompt:
Feature: live progress for recipe imports from a URL or pasted HTML/JSON.

POST /api/recipes/create/url and POST /api/recipes/create/html-or-json answer only once the whole import is done. With the scraper's stages (fetching the page, extracting the data, downloading the image, and for the AI strategies downloading a video, transcribing it and building the recipe) an import can take a minute with nothing on screen. The create page should show what is happening while it waits.

Expected:
1. Streaming twins of both endpoints at /api/recipes/create/url/stream and /api/recipes/create/html-or-json/stream, for the same authenticated users, taking the same inputs as the existing endpoints (url, or data with an optional url, plus include_tags and include_categories). They answer 200 with a server-sent event stream (text/event-stream) made of "event: <name>" and "data: <json>" lines, one blank line between events; the tests read the whole response body and parse it.
   - Progress: event "progress", data {"message": "<text>"}, sent as each stage starts. An import that goes through the web scraper emits at least one. The stages and their messages, translated backend strings under new en-US keys recipe.create-progress.*: fetching-webpage ("Fetching webpage...", only when the page really has to be fetched, so pasted HTML skips it), extracting-recipe-data, creating-recipe-from-webpage-data (the Open Graph strategy), downloading-image (only when the recipe has an image), creating-recipe-with-ai, downloading-video, transcribing-audio-with-ai and creating-recipe-from-transcript-with-ai (the AI strategies).
   - Success ends with event "done", data {"slug": "<slug of the new recipe>"}, after the recipe is created with tags and categories applied as the existing endpoints do.
   - Any exception during the import (including the scraper's bad-data HTTPException) ends the stream, still with status 200, with event "error", data {"message": "<text describing the failure>"}; nothing is created.
   - Plumbing: create_from_html(url, translator, html=None, on_progress=None) and RecipeScraper.scrape(url, html=None, on_progress=None) and each strategy's parse(on_progress=None) accept an optional async callable taking the message; with None nothing changes. The CRUD route class that copies updatedAt into the Last-Modified header must pass a streaming response through untouched.
2. The existing endpoints share the pipeline and keep their contract: 201 with the slug (declared response model str) on the done event; on an error event, 400 with an ErrorResponse body whose message is the error event's text.
3. The create pages use the stream endpoints and show the progress text (frontend, not graded).

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/integration_tests/user_recipe_tests` for quick loops; the whole backend suite is `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (about 8 minutes).
title: feat: Recipe import progress (#7252)
